Calculate quality control metrics

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/addQC.R
addQC.Rd

These functions calculate simple quality control metrics, such as library sizes, for samples or features.

addQC(x, ...)

getQC(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
addQC(x, by = "cols", ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
getQC(x, assay.type = "counts", by = "cols", ...)

Arguments

x

a SummarizedExperiment object.

...

additional arguments passed to getQC:

  • name: Specifies the names of the metrics in the result. Must have the same length as the number of metrics. (Default: c("total", "detected", "mean", "sd", "cv", "q0", "q25", "q50", "q100"))

  • na.rm: Logical scalar. Should NA values be omitted? (Default: TRUE)

by

Character scalar. Determines if metrics are calculated for samples ("cols") or features ("rows"). (Default: "cols")

assay.type

Character scalar. Specifies the name of assay used in calculation. (Default: "counts")

Value

getQC returns a DataFrame with one row per sample (or feature). addQC returns x with the metrics added to colData(x) (or rowData(x)).

Details

The following metrics are calculated for each sample (or feature):

  • total: Sum of values, e.g., library size.

  • detected: Number of values greater than zero.

  • mean: Mean of values.

  • median: Median of values.

  • sd: Standard deviation of values.

  • cv: Coefficient of variation of values.

  • q*: Quantiles. By default, 0%, 25%, 50%, and 100%

Examples

data(GlobalPatterns)
tse <- GlobalPatterns

# Calculate metrics for samples
getQC(tse)
